models.author: Scott Weeden
models.description:
# Model Summary

A 1D convolutional neural network that predicts the per-row residual `TVT - tvt_anchor` for the Rogii Wellbore Geology Prediction competition. `tvt_anchor` is the moving anchor: forward-fill of the last observed `TVT_input` value within each well. The model only contributes a small correction on top of the anchor (median per-well RMSE 8.65 ft on 5-fold well-grouped CV).

## Architecture

4 layer 1D conv (kernel=5, padding=2):
  Conv1d(in_ch, 64) -> ReLU -> Conv1d(64, 64) -> ReLU -> Conv1d(64, 32) -> ReLU -> Conv1d(32, 1)

# Model Characteristics

- Trained on the full 404-well train table.
- 17 input features (anchored_v13 set).
- Trained for 60 epochs, 2-seed ensemble averaged.
- 36,993 parameters.
- Observed rows (`TVT_input_missing == 0`) have their predicted residual clipped to 0.

# Interactive Dashboard

Version 2 now includes `well_viz.html`, an interactive HTML/JS dashboard that allows for:
- Visualization of wellbore trajectories against geological markers.
- Real-time TVT variance analysis.
- Dynamic geosteering projections with steering bias simulation and EGFD constraints.

# Data Overview

The bundle ships `test_table_for_regressionLearner.csv`, the pre-engineered feature table for the public Kaggle test wells, and the new `well_viz.html` dashboard.

instances.overview: PyTorch state_dict for a 4-layer 1D-CNN that predicts TVT-tvt_anchor residuals on top of a per-well moving anchor. Pickled bundle also contains the standardization stats (mu, sd), the feature list, and CV metadata. Companion file test_table_for_regressionLearner.csv is the pre-engineered feature table for the 3 public Kaggle test wells (loading from this guarantees feature consistency with training).
instances.usage:
# Model Format

The pickle dict has keys: `model` (None for seq), `seq_state` (state_dict + standardization + arch info), `feature_builder` ("anchored_v13"), `feature_list` (the 17 input feature names), `target_kind` ("residual"), `shrink` (1.0), `tvt_clip` (training TVT range), `cv_result`.

# Training Data

The full Kaggle competition train table (404 wells, 2.6M rows) pre-engineered with the standard Rogii feature pipeline (GR imputation, rolling stats, typewell at anchor TVT).

# Model Inputs

For each well sequence: 17 features (see `feature_list` in pickle). Standardize with the saved `mu`, `sd` before feeding to the network.

# Model Outputs

Per-row prediction = `tvt_anchor + shrink * model_residual`, with observed rows (TVT_input_missing == 0) clipped to anchor.

# Model Usage

See the inference notebook for the full pipeline. Standardize -> per-well forward pass -> add anchor -> observed-row clip -> clip to train TVT range -> merge with sample_submission ids.

# Fine-tuning

Not tuned for fine-tuning. To retrain from scratch use the harness at `exp_harness.py` in the local repo.

# Changelog

v1 (2026-05-19): initial release. CV mean 12.69 ft, per-well median 8.65 ft.

## [Locus](https://antfriend.github.io/locus_arxiv.pdf)
# Locus: Synthetic Perceptual Modeling

We present Locus, a framework for synthetic perceptual modeling — representing experiential knowledge as a typed graph of perceptual transitions, each anchored to a perceiving agent’s subjective worldview (umwelt). Locus introduces @LATxLON geographic coordinate addressing: an authority-free scheme in which every knowledge node is identified by a deterministic latitude/longitude pair requiring no registry, no network connectivity, and no external authority.
Knowledge is stored as toot-bits organized in TTDB (MyMentalPalaceDB), a flat Markdown
or LaTeX knowledge graph traversable without a database engine. The framework’s foundational epistemic primitive is the @PERCEPT paired node: a before/after transition record that encodes what a perceptual shift was like for a specific agent, not merely that it occurred. Records carry optional Toot-Bit Epistemic Weight (TBEW) blocks — confidence, revision count, salience, and recency — from which a derived Epistemic Priority Score (EPS) identifies high uncertainty, high-salience nodes as primary attention targets, providing a lightweight symbolic approximation of free-energy minimization. The Locus specification suite spans 20 RFCs across four suites: TTDB (knowledge graph format, cursor semantics, typed edges, epistemic weight, experiential perception), TTN (semantic mesh network with trust, compression, and LoRa framing), TTCP (web publishing and interactive 3D globe visualization), and A32 (ESP32 autonomous device framework). Agents on ESP32-class hardware execute deterministic sense-reason-act
loops from local TTDB storage — no cloud inference required. We provide a 21-node affective knowledge graph grounded in hippocampal-prefrontal emotional embedding research, and a complete open-source reference implementation. All specifications and firmware are publicly available. 

## Usage: [See the Quick Start](https://antfriend.github.io/share/companion.html)
